digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate (necessity criterion + bug review tier)
propositions: The plan-review gate has no criterion checking whether a proposed change is actually needed, missing the FixedBench over-action gap.
A new pass-1 advisory criterion `necessity` flags plans that neither reproduce nor motivate the change, while passing well-motivated, no-op, or docs-only plans.
Bug tickets short-circuit to a bare exempt-PASS with zero substantive plan review; a light advisory tier should run the DET floor plus necessity instead.
Both pieces ship advisory (never block): `necessity` registered non-orphan in CANONICAL_LLM and the bug tier downgrades DET findings to advisory with empty det_blocking.
The E2 class-4 unnecessary-mechanism mutant corpus does not exist, so the original retrospective gate is unrunnable; validation instead uses bounded hand-authored fixtures via `rebar criteria eval`.
Bug 5886 serves the bug-tier lifecycle fixture (a real bug that got only exempt-PASS) but not the necessity positive, since its plan already demonstrates need with reproduction steps.
